summary: Standing operational rules for the PR drain: dispatch cleans .ai-sdlc-only Step 10.5 stops, reaps stale claims, sweeps red PRs, applies DEC-0142 to incomplete reviewer sets, without a planner round trip

options.description: Dispatch applies the five rules below from main, class (a), for every task; the planner is consulted only for a real source conflict, a review finding, or a shape not listed
Each occurrence gets its own planner record (today's practice: DEC-0153, 0155, 0156 plus four relayed rulings dispatch could not act on)

body:
Operator context 2026-10-13 (Dominique): the drain is the open PR list; PRs sat for hours because every mechanical stop needed a planner record and dispatch correctly refused relayed messages as authority (hard rule 10). This record makes the rulings the planner gave by message today authority on main. Class (a): each rule is reversible, task-local, and loosens no hook, gate, review or attestation control (the hook still re-signs, the full reviewer set still runs, nothing is force-pushed, no board file is hand-edited).

Rule 1 (Step 10.5 dirty .ai-sdlc tree; generalises DEC-0153): when next-step stops at Step 10.5 with rebase-conflict and git status in the task worktree shows changes only under .ai-sdlc/ (attestations, transcript-leaves, _decisions, reviews, verdicts) and no conflicting source file, dispatch commits them as one chore commit (deleted stale envelopes included; the pre-push hook re-signs), then re-queues the task rebase-first; if the patch-id changes, with the DEC-0142 hand-review path; never a developer pass when reviews already approved.

Rule 2 (incomplete reviewer set; reading of DEC-0142): a verifier or attestation-sign refusal naming an incomplete reviewer set, missing leaves for the current patch-id, or a changed patch-id is the DEC-0142 stop; dispatch re-queues with the full three-reviewer hand-review note. A failure record with an empty cause whose notes mention reviewer set, leaves or patch-id is the same stop.

Rule 3 (stale claims; RFC-0041 OQ-3 until AISDLC-826 lands): an inflight claim with no heartbeat for 30 minutes and no verdict, whose holder session is idle, gone or unknown, is reaped by dispatch: failed verdict cause stale-worker, release, clear and relaunch the executor, re-queue with the step it stalled at.

Rule 4 (red PR sweep; until AISDLC-829 lands): each tick dispatch lists open non-draft PRs; any with a red required check, CONFLICTING, or CHANGES_REQUESTED that is not queued or inflight is re-queued with the matching note (attestation red: DEC-0142; conflict: rebase-first; Build and Test red: fix the named suite; cancelled superseded run: re-push). A CHANGES_REQUESTED whose body is the CI reviewer 'Review agent failed: Anthropic API error 401' is dismissed with that documented reason (CLAUDE.md permits dismissing stale reviews for API errors). PRs with no task id are reported to the planner each tick, never resumed, never closed.

Rule 5 (sequencing): a PR whose only red is the five-step DoR Gate-2 finding waits for AISDLC-828 to land before its re-queue; AISDLC-742 (#1248) and 651.2 (#1345) are the current cases, 742 is covered by Rule 1 now and re-queued after 828.

Five-step: requirement questioned = 'every mechanical stop needs a planner record' (set by hard rule 10 read per occurrence); deleted = the per-occurrence round trip; nothing added beyond this record. Velocity impact: positive; today it would have saved seven round trips and roughly six hours of PR idle time.
